svg.title: PGD-3 advantage comes from which coordinates it perturbs
svg.desc: Panel A: mean source-context margin drop for FGSM and three matched-count subsets, development vs confirmation. Panel B: per-group PGD-3 subset damage against matched random subsets.
svg.text: Same coordinate count, different coordinates: PGD-3 picks damaging ones, gradient saliency picks weak ones
Qwen3-VL-2B (bf16), ε = 1/255, official 8-bit scoring. Source-context margin drop, pooled over the two source contexts. Unit = counterfactual group (n = 48 per split).
the k coords of FGSM's support
Share of the PGD−FGSM gap explained by sparsity: development 0.08 [0.01, 0.14]; confirmation 0.03 [-0.02, 0.09]
B · Per group: PGD-3 subset vs matched random
random subset, mean of 8 seeds (margin drop)

Subsets are masks of FGSM's own rounded perturbation with exactly k = |PGD-3 support| RGB channel coordinates; k is matched per group and source. Hover a mark for values.
